agent_role: SHA-512/SHA-384/BLAKE2 from-scratch implementer for ProofBundle crypto-core
task_description: Implement SHA-512 and SHA-384 (FIPS 180-4) and BLAKE2b/BLAKE2s (RFC 7693) from scratch in pure JavaScript for crypto-core/, matching the house style established by crypto-core/sha256.mjs and crypto-core/keccak.mjs. Hard constraint: the implementation files (sha512.mjs, blake2.mjs) import no cryptographic library whatsoever (no noble-*, no WebCrypto, no node:crypto) -- only node:crypto in the *.test.mjs files, used strictly as an independent verification yardstick alongside hardcoded published known-answer values. Write and run the corresponding test files until they pass with zero failures, then produce signed provenance for the work.

external_references_used.title: FIPS 180-4: Secure Hash Standard (SHS)
external_references_used.use: SHA-512 / SHA-384 algorithm specification (sections 4.2.3, 5.1.2, 5.3.4, 5.3.5, 6.4, 6.5). K/H0 constants were not transcribed from this document; they were derived from first principles (fractional parts of cube/square roots of primes, via exact BigInt integer sqrt/cbrt) and cross-validated by reproducing SHA-256's own K/H0 with the same method and diffing against crypto-core/sha256.mjs.

external_references_used.title: NIST/FIPS 180-4 SHA-384/SHA-512 test vectors
external_references_used.use: Hardcoded known-answer values in sha512.test.mjs (empty string, 'abc', the 112-character multi-block message, one million 'a' characters, for both SHA-384 and SHA-512). Each value was independently cross-verified against a live node:crypto computation before being hardcoded.

external_references_used.title: RFC 7693: The BLAKE2 Cryptographic Hash and Message Authentication Code (MAC)
external_references_used.use: BLAKE2b/BLAKE2s algorithm specification -- fetched and read directly (not from memory) for the SIGMA permutation table (section 2.7), mixing function G (3.1), compression function F (3.2), parameter block layout (2.5), and block/padding/counter rules (3.3). Appendix A and B worked examples ('abc') hardcoded as known-answer values.

external_references_used.title: Official BLAKE2 reference implementation test vectors
external_references_used.use: Downloaded directly (3072 entries). Verified its unkeyed entries reproduce node:crypto's output exactly (confirming authenticity), then used its keyed entries -- which node:crypto cannot verify in this environment -- as an independent oracle, including several hardcoded in blake2.test.mjs at block-boundary lengths.

external_references_used.title: golang.org/x/crypto blake2s and blake2b test vectors
external_references_used.use: Downloaded directly. Used the hashes128 table (BLAKE2s New128: keyed, 16-byte output) as an independently published known-answer set for a non-default BLAKE2s output length, hardcoded in blake2.test.mjs.

external_references_used.title: Python 3.14 hashlib.blake2b (CPython _blake2 C extension)
external_references_used.use: Used as a live, independent (non-Node) oracle to generate several BLAKE2b known-answer values at non-default output lengths (1, 16, 20, 48 bytes) and a keyed+short-output combination, hardcoded in blake2.test.mjs. hashlib.blake2s was found to crash with an unrelated native 'Illegal instruction' fault in this specific environment and was not used.

external_references_used.title: node:crypto (Node v24.18.0 / OpenSSL 3.5.7)
external_references_used.use: Primary live verification yardstick in both *.test.mjs files, per the task's required design: createHash('sha512'/'sha384'/'blake2b512'/'blake2s256'). Used only in test files, never in the implementation files.

environment_notes: node:crypto's createHash('blake2b512', { outputLength: N }) throws 'not XOF or invalid length' in this environment, and the { key } option is silently ignored (verified with a deliberately oversized, spec-invalid key that produced byte-identical output to no key at all). This is why blake2.test.mjs leans on hardcoded published/independent vectors for keyed and non-default-length coverage rather than a live Node check for those cases.
